figures.finding: Belize's Labour Act makes a child a person under fourteen and bars employing a child under twelve, during school hours, before 6 a.m. or after 8 p.m., for more than two hours on a school day or a Sunday, or in work injurious to health or schooling (s. 169); no child under fourteen may work in an industrial undertaking (s. 164); the Minister may set further rules by regulation (s. 170). So work is open from twelve with these limits, and fully from fourteen; the US Department of Labor's 2024 report reads the floor as fourteen, its 2020 report as twelve.
figures.applies: Belize (Labour Act as revised to 31 December 2020).

sources.said: “child” means a person who is under the age of fourteen years;

no child shall be employed– (a) so long as he is under the age of twelve years; (b) before the close of school hours on any day on which he is required to attend school; (c) before six o’clock in the morning or after eight o’clock in the evening on any day; (d) for more than two hours on any day on which he is required to attend school; (e) for more than two hours on any Sunday;
no person shall employ a child in a public or private industrial undertaking or in a branch thereof.
However, the country did not also raise its minimum working age, which remains at 14.

figures.finding: Belize's age of majority is eighteen: the Interpretation Act makes an adult any person who has attained eighteen, and the Families and Children Act makes a child, unless a law says otherwise, a person below eighteen.

value.law: Interpretation Act Cap 1, s. 3 ('adult'); Families and Children Act Cap 173, s. 2 ('child')

sources.said: “adult” means any person who has attained the age of eighteen years;
“child” means, unless provided otherwise in any law, a person below the age of eighteen years;

figures.finding: Belize has no licence for child performers: a child (under fourteen) in paid performing work is held to the Labour Act's general limits (no work under twelve, none in school hours or outside 6 a.m. to 8 p.m., two hours at most on a school day or a Sunday, s. 169), and the only performing rule is a saving that lets a child appear without fee in an entertainment whose proceeds go to a charitable or educational purpose, free of the two-hour cap and any regulations (s. 171); the Families and Children Act bars any work detrimental to a child's health, education or development (s. 7). No schooling, chaperone or rest-day rule exists for sets, and nothing distinguishes writing or directing.

sources.said: Nothing in sections 170(1)(c) or 169(d) or in any regulations shall prevent a child from taking part without fee or reward in an entertainment, the net proceeds of which are devoted to any charitable or educational purpose or to any purpose other than the private profit of the promoters.
(d) for more than two hours on any day on which he is required to attend school; (e) for more than two hours on any Sunday;
no child shall be employed or engaged in any activity that may be detrimental to his health, education, or mental, physical or moral development.

figures.finding: In Belize a person under eighteen may make a contract of service on their own (Labour Act s. 31), though no damages for its breach can be recovered from a child or young person, and may sue for wages as if of full age (Families and Children Act s. 13); other contracts follow the Contract Act's infants' rules (loans and goods other than necessaries void, s. 12). No court approval and no set-aside of a minor's earnings is required, and nothing separates performing from writing or directing work.

figures.finding: Under the Belize Companies Act 2022 an individual under eighteen is disqualified from appointment as a company's director (s. 102(1)(a)), and a company is incorporated only through a registered agent (s. 6(2)); the Act sets no age for a shareholder, so a minor may hold shares in a producer's company but direct it only from eighteen.
figures.applies: Belize (domestic companies; IBCs under Cap 270 not read).

sources.said: The following are disqualified for appointment as the director of a company– (a) an individual who is under eighteen years of age;
an application for the incorporation of a company may be filed only by the Registered Agent

figures.finding: Belize has no film fund of its own; the National Institute of Culture and History's Belize Culture Fund gives small grants (up to $5,000) to Belizean individuals, filmmakers among them, and to organisations including film production companies, one application per cycle, and sets no applicant age; its application form asks no age or date of birth.
